selectionPolicy: Frequency orders candidate review; it does not assign a JLPT level.
Resolve existing spellings, readings, compositional forms and meanings before adding SRS units.
Classify usage, register and learning focus separately from introduction level.
Require direct beginner teaching evidence (a standalone word-list headword or an explicitly taught expression) and everyday usefulness; record the evidence type.
Irodori through Elementary 2 is an approximate N4 ability benchmark, not an official word-by-word JLPT classification.
Marugoto A2 and publisher N4 curricula support an editorial N4 supplement; neither assigns an official JLPT level to individual words. A2/B1 evidence alone is insufficient for this batch.
New entries are supplemental and share the existing N4 daily introduction budget.
Author original English/French meanings and examples; do not copy source sentences, illustrations or audio.
Keep unverified levels unassigned; pending-review and deferred do not mean that a word is unimportant. A recommendation does not itself create an SRS item.

followupReviews.description: Ten candidates reviewed in frequency order: the six recommendations were subsequently imported as N4 supplements in batch 2; four remain deferred.
followupReviews.searchLimits: Positive headword evidence is recorded below; unsuccessful searches are not proof that a word is advanced. The TRY! evidence comes from indexed publisher PDFs, as detailed in each source access note.

followupReviews.description: Review the six agreed everyday candidates in frequency order: import 父親, 冗談 and 実は; defer 母親, つまり and 平気 without assigning an introduction level.
followupReviews.searchLimits: An unsuccessful search is not proof of advanced difficulty. Record each publisher placement as its own curriculum choice; do not infer an official JLPT level or a harder meaning from the asymmetric parent-word labels.
